records.text: Jerri Frantzve worked for the DuPont family as director of employee relations
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I kid you not. She starts working for the DuPont family, becoming the director of employee relations for DuPont because she's so good at psychology.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Current source searches did not locate a reliable employment record confirming Jerri Frantzve served as DuPont's director of employee relations.

records.text: DuPont completed what was then the largest corporate merger in history with Conoco in 1983
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: In 1983, DuPont completes the largest merger in corporate history with Conoco Oil, and they're able to do this thanks to Reagan and George Bush being in office, deregulating things, making it easier for private corporations to go in and do bigger deals.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. A contemporaneous federal court opinion describes the DuPont-Conoco merger as occurring in summer 1981 and as the largest merger to that date, directly contradicting the claimed 1983 date.

sources.title: Conoco Inc. v. United States
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous federal opinion dates the DuPont-Conoco merger to summer 1981.

records.speaker: Vanity Fair

verification.notes: Public court-based reporting confirms Robert H. Richards IV pleaded guilty to fourth-degree rape of his daughter, who was three at the time of the abuse, and was sentenced in 2009. records.text: Dominick Dunne reported that money for the killing traced back to the DuPont family and that it appeared Lisa Dean and Christopher Moseley had the victim killed.
records.speaker: Dominick Dunne

appearances.snippet: And as Dominick Dunne reported in Vanity Fair, the money traced back to the DuPont family. It appeared that Lisa Dean—who is a DuPont—didn't approve of her drug-addicted son dating a drug-addicted Vegas sex worker. So she and her husband, Christopher Moseley, had her killed.

verification.notes: Contemporary court reporting confirms that Christopher Moseley, husband of DuPont heiress Lisa Dean Moseley, contracted for Patricia Margello’s murder and pleaded guilty. It does not establish Candace’s stronger assertion that Lisa jointly had Margello killed. The canonical name is Moseley, correcting the transcript/legacy Mosley error. Legacy verification history remains in provenance.

sources.title: Heiress’ Husband Sentenced in Murder of Ex-Prostitute
sources.relevance: Contemporary court reporting identifies Christopher Moseley as Lisa Dean Moseley’s husband and records his guilty plea in the Patricia Margello murder-for-hire conspiracy.

sources.title: Plot hatched after failure to extricate du Pont heir from relationship
sources.relevance: Contemporary reporting says Moseley contracted for Margello’s killing and pleaded guilty; it does not establish that Lisa Dean Moseley jointly ordered the murder.

records.text: Vanity Fair reported that a Las Vegas sex worker's decomposing body was found in a motel air conditioner and that she had been killed by three hired hands.
records.speaker: Vanity Fair

appearances.snippet: Two years later, the decomposing body of a Las Vegas prostitute was found stuffed in the air conditioner of a seedy motel. She was killed by three hired hands.
